title: Resolve misaligned usage attribution for sub-organizations when API keys are reissued
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Finance flagged intermittent misbilling where API usage from sub-organizations (sub-accounts) is attributed to the wrong tenant or marked as orphaned shortly after API key reissue/rotation. Root cause appears tied to how the metering pipeline and rate limiter resolve tenant attribution when key metadata is changing during rotation and sub-account hierarchies exist.
reproduction_steps: Create parent org P and sub-org S with independent API key scoping
Issue request traffic from a client using S's API key while concurrently rotating keys for S (simulate automated rotation within 1-2s window)
Observe usage records in the metrics pipeline (raw events/ingest) and downstream billing aggregation
Compare attribution between immediate ingestion (raw events), rate limiter logs, and the billing ledger after 1 minute and after 24 hours
observed_behavior: A subset (~0.5-2%) of tokens/requests from sub-org S are attributed to parent org P or show up as unassigned in the billing ledger. Rate limiter logs show decisions keyed by the rotated API key identifier before the auth-service mapping fully propagated. Reconciliation job later fixes some, but not all, leaving discrepancies in billing exports.
expected_behavior: All usage generated under sub-org S should be attributed to S throughout the pipeline (real-time rate-limiting, metrics, and final billing ledger) despite key rotation events. Any transient state must be handled deterministically and reconciled automatically without leaving orphaned charges.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: finance -> SE -> ENG reported on 2026-02-26; reproduced in staging with synthetic traffic
Logs show the auth-service emits two events during rotation: 'key_deactivate' then 'key_create' with reused short_key_id in some flows (legacy compatibility).

Metering ingest uses short_key_id as primary tenant lookup in the fast path (for performance). When rotation occurs, the short_key_id briefly maps to parent org P in the tenant-index cache while downstream services read older mapping snapshots.
Rate limiter uses the same fast-path lookup leading to token allowance decisions and counters incremented under inconsistent tenant id for overlapping windows.

Root cause: a combination of (1) reuse of non-globally-unique short key identifier during rotation for compatibility, (2) eventual consistency between auth-service and tenant-index cache, and (3) downstream services prioritizing low-latency short_key lookup without fallback to authoritative key_uuid lookup.

Edge case: sub-accounts that inherit some parent metadata but keep separate billing profiles are especially affected because reconciliation heuristics prefer latest-seen tenant mapping, which can flip during rotation.
Scope estimate: affects ~0.5-2% of rotations in heavy-rotate customers; potential revenue mismatch and quota enforcement anomalies.
Relevant traces: rate-limiter trace IDs RL-20260227-1a2b (attached to PR), ingest spans show tenant-id=null at 2026-02-27T15:42:10Z for a 30s window.
Confirmed that not all misattributions are auto-corrected by the existing reconciliation job; some entries never join final ledger due to late-arriving attribution metadata.
Discussed migration constraints with Product: cannot pause rotations; fix must be backward compatible and low-latency for the hot path.
proposed_fix: Make key_uuid the canonical identifier used by metering and rate-limiter fast path; short_key_id can remain for display but must not be relied on for tenant attribution.
Update auth-service to emit a short-lived 'rotation in-progress' flag so downstream services avoid ambiguous attribution windows and fall back to authoritative key_uuid lookup.
Modify tenant-index cache to support versioned mappings and an atomic swap semantics during rotation so lookups either see old or new mapping but not an inconsistent interim mapping.
Add a reconciliation component to reprocess a 48-hour window of events for rotated keys and re-attribute any orphaned usage; write migration script to patch billing ledger where feasible.
Ensure rate-limiter counters are dual-written during rollout (tenant-id by short_key and by key_uuid) and drain old counters after safe cutover to prevent double-charging.
Avoid short_key reuse going forward; reserve short_key namespace per key_uuid or introduce namespaced short IDs.
Document compatibility changes and provide a rollout plan for Dedicated/Private deployments that may have cached auth-state.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Change metering fast-path in staging and a small subset of customers to prefer key_uuid; monitor attribution delta; keep dual-write enabled.
Phase 2 (controlled): Enable auth-service 'rotation-in-progress' flag and update tenant-index atomic swap in production for 10% of rotations; run re-attribution job for affected windows.
Phase 3 (full): Flip default to canonical key_uuid in rate-limiter and metering, disable short_key fast-path after a 2-week observation window, and run ledger migration for remaining discrepancies.
Rollback plan: revert dual-write and switch back to previous fast-path; disable new reconciliation job if unexpected high impact observed.
Post-deploy verification: compare pre/post attribution counts, finance reconciliation, and run sampled customer audits for top 20 affected orgs.
test_plan: Unit tests: ensure tenant-index lookup returns key_uuid-backed tenant id and falls back correctly when mappings change
Integration tests: end-to-end with auth-service rotation workflow, ensure metering, rate-limiter, and billing ingest preserve tenant id under concurrent rotation
Load tests: simulate high-frequency rotations + synthetic traffic to measure latency impact and verify no measurable increase in tail-latency
Regression tests: backfill test asserting that reconciliation job catches previously orphaned events
Customer sandbox validation: invite two power customers to run rotations during scheduled maintenance and validate ledger reconciliation.
monitoring_changes: New dashboard: 'key-rotation-attribution-variance' showing live percentage of events with differing tenant attribution across fast-path vs authoritative path
Alert: >0.2% orphaned-attribution over 1 hour triggers P0 pager to engineering oncall and billing ownership
Add tracing tags to rate-limiter and ingest pipeline to correlate tenant mapping source (short_key vs key_uuid) and rotation flag
Daily reconciliation job health status and re-attribution counts metric exposed to Finance and SRE.
